_what: H3 for the filter grammar (#896 task 2): every group of phrases on which packages/tagger/src/grammar/filter.ts and parseSubject disagree, grouped by the SubjectFilter fields that differ, over packages/tagger/phrases.jsonl. Each group is labelled after reading EVERY member, not a sample. 'grammar right' cites the rule or the printed text; 'grammar wrong' must be fixed before task 3 switches derive over; 'both wrong' says what neither reads. phrase-diff-triage.test.ts fails when a group appears, disappears or changes size, and when the parsed count moves, so a change to either parser is re-triaged and banked here.

control.label: grammar right
control.why: Two shapes, both right. (1) 'spells you cast' (70 of 73): a spell's controller is the player who put it on the stack, so the caster is the controller -- parseSubject's control regex knows 'you control' and 'your' but not 'you cast', and answered any. (2) 'of an opponent's choice' / 'of your choice' (6): the chooser is not the controller; parseSubject read 'opponent'/'your' anywhere and answered opp/you. A Clue, Food or Treasure 'of your choice' is created under the creator's control by CONTROLLER_DEFAULT, not by this word. The 'that targets only' member names the TARGET's controller, not the spell's, and the subject is refused (restricted) either way. 'a token that's a copy of a permanent you control': 'you control' names the ORIGINAL, not the token, which CONTROLLER_DEFAULT gives its creator (CR 111.2). (3) the quote leak of #1387 is fixed: parseSubject now cuts a token's quoted ability before it reads any field, so the Prydwen's Knight ("... under your control this turn.") agrees with the grammar and left this group.

scope.label: grammar right
scope.why: (1) 'creatures target player controls', 'a creature target opponent controls': the player is the target, the creatures are not -- parseSubject's scope reads 'target' anywhere in the string. (2) 'any number of targets', 'one or two targets': parseSubject's \btarget\b misses the plural. (3) 'a creature each opponent controls': the quantifier binds the opponent. (4) Two token names ('Kobolds of Kher Keep', 'Llanowar Elves'): a plural in a NAME is not a mass subject. (5) 'a token that's a copy of target creature': the original is targeted, the token is created, not targeted. Copy tokens of a target ('a token that's a copy of target artifact') are not themselves targeted.

fromZone,scope.label: grammar right
fromZone,scope.why: 'a nonland card from target opponent's hand' (Thoughtseize family): the target is the opponent, not the card, and the card comes from a hand. parseSubject's ORIGIN_ZONE allows only a|an|your|their|the before the zone, so a possessive player ('target opponent's', 'each opponent's') drops the zone, and its scope reads the player's 'target'.

other.label: grammar right
other.why: 'up to one other target creature', 'one or more other creatures', 'any number of other permanents': 'other' after a count. parseSubject's `other` regex accepts at most one word before it. Also 'target creature other than this creature', 'all creatures other than this creature': the same fact as 'another' written out.

fromZone.label: grammar right
fromZone.why: 'target card from an opponent's graveyard', '... from defending player's graveyard': the same ORIGIN_ZONE possessive gap as the fromZone,scope group, where the possessive carries no 'target'. Also 'lands from the top of your library' and 'creature spells from the top of your library' (Courser/Future Sight family: the origin is the library), and 'up to two target cards from a single graveyard' / 'from graveyards' / 'from all graveyards' (the cards come from a graveyard; 'single' constrains how many graveyards, not the class). parseSubject's ORIGIN_ZONE reads none of these.

zone.label: grammar right
zone.why: 'target creature card in your graveyard', 'all cards in your hand': `zone` is where the subject lives and absent means the battlefield (schema), so parseSubject's reading puts every one of these on the battlefield. TASK 3 CAUTION: on a producer, zone graveyard is read as a graveyard FILL by graveyardFillMatches; the switch must check each consumer of `zone` before trusting this field from the grammar. The two OR-lists whose alternatives have different heads ('target spell, nonland permanent, or card in a graveyard', 'an artifact or a card in your hand') are refused, not zoned. Also 'Enchant creature card in a graveyard' (Animate Dead's enchant line, CR 303.4a) and 'cards in graveyards' (plural).

The 'that targets only a single Golem' member is refused (restricted) either way.

The cross-slot OR split lives in the type/subtype path only; an OR whose branches differ on a status is not split there. Every member read.
